title: CoSA: The Conflict of Skills Attack in Real-World LLM Agent Ecosystems
abstract: arXiv:2610.35082v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Agent Skills allow LLM agents to combine reusable capabilities, but checking each Skill in isolation cannot rule out policy violations when they are composed. We term such failures Conflict of Skills (CoS): artifacts or assessment signals produced for one purpose may be reused downstream without preserving the restrictions or authorization needed for their new use. Using controlled executions of publicly available Skills and matched single-Skill controls, we identify four recurring mechanisms behind CoS. Building on these findings, we introduce the Conflict of Skills Attack (CoSA), which adds locally admitted Skills to an existing pool to supply missing business operations (capability supplementation) or reshape artifact exchange, decision reuse, and target/action bindings (relationship reshaping). translated_title: CoSA：真实世界LLM智能体生态系统中的技能冲突攻击
translated_abstract: 智能体技能使LLM智能体能够组合可复用的能力，但仅对每个技能进行孤立检查，无法排除它们在组合使用时出现的策略违规。我们将此类失败称为技能冲突：为某一目的而产生的人工制品或评估信号可能在下游被复用，却没有保留其新用途所需的限制或授权。通过对公开可用技能的受控执行以及匹配的单技能对照实验，我们识别出CoS背后四种反复出现的机制。基于这些发现，我们提出了技能冲突攻击，它通过向现有技能池中添加本地准入的技能，来提供缺失的业务操作（能力补充），或重塑人工制品交换、决策复用以及目标/行动绑定（关系重塑）。CoSA不会改变现有的技能和运行时权限。为了在自主技能选择条件下评估这一威胁，我们引入了CoSA-
tldr: 本文提出“技能冲突”（CoS）概念及CoSA攻击方法，证明仅通过向LLM智能体技能池添加本地准入的新技能（进行能力补充或关系重塑），就能在技能组合使用时引发策略违规，且无需改动现有技能或运行时权限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Conflict of Skills (CoS) concept and the CoSA attack, showing that merely adding locally admitted Skills to an LLM agent's existing pool—through capability supplementation or relationship reshaping—can trigger policy violations when Skills are composed, without modifying existing Skills or runtime permissions.
